record.original_question: Can one analyze solutions of the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation simultaneously at more than one space-time point, rather than only through one-point statistics?

evidence.quote: Another open problem is to analyze solutions of KPZ at more than one space-time point.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) stochastic partial differential equation
$$\partial_t h(t,x) = \tfrac{1}{2}\partial_x^2 h(t,x) + \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_x h(t,x))^2 + \xi(t,x), \qquad t>0,\ x\in\mathbb{R},$$
where $\xi$ is space-time white noise on $\mathbb{R}_{>0}\times\mathbb{R}$, and the equation is interpreted in the Hopf–Cole (or regularity-structures) sense. For an initial condition $h(0,\cdot)=h_0$ (e.g. narrow-wedge, flat, or stationary), let $h(t,x)$ denote the corresponding solution.

Develop a tractable description of the joint law of the random vector
$$\bigl(h(t_1,x_1),\,h(t_2,x_2),\,\dots,\,h(t_n,x_n)\bigr)$$
at an arbitrary finite collection of space-time points $\{(t_i,x_i)\}_{i=1}^n$ with $n\ge 2$ (in particular at distinct times $t_i$), going beyond the well-studied one-point statistics. Concretely, obtain explicit formulas (e.g. Fredholm determinant or integrable-operator representations) for the multi-point distribution function
$$\mathbb{P}\bigl(h(t_1,x_1)\le s_1,\ \dots,\ h(t_n,x_n)\le s_n\bigr),$$
and analyze its properties, for general initial data.
artifact.status_search_result: Significant progress has been made on multi-point space-time statistics of the KPZ universality class. Multi-point distributions of the KPZ fixed point are known explicitly for narrow-wedge and flat initial data, and two-point formulas exist for half-Brownian and Brownian data. A 2025 work derives space-time joint distribution formulas for the KPZ fixed point with general compactly supported initial data via a 1:2:3 scaling limit of TASEP. Corresponding multi-point formulas directly for the KPZ equation (pre-limit) at general initial data remain less complete, so the problem is partially solved rather than fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Multipoint distributions of the KPZ fixed point with compactly supported initial conditions
status_evidence.snippet: A formula for the space-time joint distributions of the KPZ fixed point with general initial conditions of compact support is obtained via the 1:2:3 KPZ scaling limit of TASEP multipoint formulas.
status_evidence.claim: Multi-point space-time distributions of the KPZ fixed point have been obtained for general compactly supported initial data.

status_evidence.title: KPZ limit theorems (Baik, ICM 2022)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys multi-time and multi-point distributions in the KPZ class, with explicit formulas for narrow-wedge and flat initial conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Multi-point KPZ-class distributions are known in several cases but not in full generality.

status_evidence.title: KPZ fixed point - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Describes the KPZ fixed point as a Markov process whose finite-dimensional distributions admit Fredholm determinant formulas.
status_evidence.claim: Finite-dimensional distributions of the KPZ fixed point admit Fredholm determinant representations.
